newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate plunges on demand, speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate plunges on demand, speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates fell sharply to end down 275 basis points on Thursday at 17.25 percent amid heavy demand for paper and late speculative dealing, traders said.
"The slide was due to players with large positions in paper," said a trader, who added that Cetes rates had also fallen so as to widen a previously narrow spread between government and bank rates.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile declined 40 basis points to end at 19.60 percent.
Traders added that Banco de Mexico participation also helped set the trend for lower secondary market rates.

The central bank drained 3.710 billion pesos from the system through a combination of direct Cetes sales and repos. One of the repos, for 260 million pesos, was assigned overnight at a low rate of 18.00 percent.
"Those who hung on to their cash to try to sway Banco de Mexico were forced to dump it later and at very low rates," another trader said.
Dealers noted, however, that the central bank assigned its longer term repos and direct sales at much higher rates, of up to 24.21 percent, in response to a late gain in U.S. long bond yields.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 17/32 to yield 7.13 percent in late trade.
Liquidity of 4.699 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Friday from prior central bank participation.
